q: Carbon is tetravalent because it has:
explanation: Carbon has atomic number 6 with electronic configuration 2,4. It has 4 valence electrons and thus forms 4 covalent bonds (tetravalent).
Catenation is the ability of carbon to form long chains by bonding with other carbon atoms. This leads to millions of carbon compounds.

q: Which allotrope of carbon is the hardest substance?
explanation: Diamond is the hardest natural substance. Each carbon is bonded to 4 others in a tetrahedral 3D structure, making it extremely hard.
Graphite has layered structure with delocalized electrons between layers. These free electrons can move, allowing graphite to conduct electricity.

q: What is the general formula of alkanes?
explanation: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with single bonds only. For n carbons, they have 2n+2 hydrogens (e.g., CH<sub>4</sub>, C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>).

q: Which gas is produced when methane burns in excess oxygen?
explanation: Combustion of methane: CH<sub>4</sub> + 2O<sub>2</sub> → CO<sub>2</sub> + 2H<sub>2</sub>O. Hydrocarbons produce CO<sub>2</sub> and H<sub>2</sub>O on burning.
The hydroxyl group (-OH) is the functional group of alcohols. Examples: methanol (CH<sub>3</sub>OH), ethanol (CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH).

q: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures are called:
explanation: Isomers have same molecular formula but different structural arrangements. For example, butane has straight and branched chain isomers.

q: Fullerene (C<sub>60</sub>) has a structure similar to:
explanation: Fullerene C<sub>60</sub> has a spherical cage structure resembling a soccer ball (buckminsterfullerene). It is used in nanotechnology.
Members of a homologous series differ by CH<sub>2</sub> group (one carbon and two hydrogens). This increases molecular mass by 14 units.
